deviations: Probit columns report the average marginal effect (dP/dT averaged over the estimation sample) of the synthetic probability; the paper does not say whether its marginal effects are averaged or evaluated at the means.

Samples and the treatment use the flags/variables shipped in data/final-data.dta (base_sample, marital_rates_sample, syntheticT, cOut, mheir, fmissmatch, fmissmatch2, fdown, celibacy, distlondon); the synthetic probability was not rebuilt from the 1815-1830 benchmark cohort. Sample sizes with a family seat (484, 260, 565) and SD of T (7.3) agree with figures stated in the paper text.

Standard errors (printed for information only, not scored) are clustered by birth year (byear), which has 22 distinct values in the data versus G = 21 stated in the paper; bootstrap-t p-values were not computed.
notes: Blind independent reproduction of Goni (2022) Table 2, Panels A and B. Controls: duke/marquess/earl daughter (pr4), English peerage (hengpee), birth order excluding heirs (biorder); Panel B adds distlondon. Probit (glm probit link) for married a commoner, married an heir, married down, never married; OLS (fixest) for absolute and husband-minus-wife landholdings percentile-rank differences. Landholdings sample = baseline women with non-missing fmissmatch (324; 260 with a seat). Never-married outcome = celibacy in the marital-rates sample (765). attempt-1 and attempt-2 were exploratory (variable listing, sample checks); they print no RESULT lines. No author scripts or result files were opened (none appeared in the mount besides .mxd map files, which were not read).
